papers.title: MoReBench: A Comprehensive Moral Reasoning Benchmark for LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces MoReBench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating moral reasoning in LLMs across multiple ethical frameworks and cultural contexts, with fine-grained evaluation metrics.

papers.title: Staircase of Ethics: Evaluating Multi-Level Moral Reasoning in LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes a multi-level evaluation framework for LLM moral reasoning organized as an ethical staircase from basic harm recognition to complex moral dilemma resolution.

papers.title: Knowing But Not Doing: ValAct-15k Benchmark for Value-Action Gaps in LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces ValAct-15k, a 15,000-scenario benchmark measuring the gap between LLMs knowing moral principles and acting on them, revealing systematic value-action gaps across models.

papers.title: UniMoral: A Universal Moral Reasoning Benchmark
papers.abstract_snippet: Presents UniMoral, a universal benchmark for moral reasoning that covers diverse ethical traditions and cultural contexts, enabling cross-framework evaluation of LLM moral competence.

papers.title: Large language models show amplified cognitive biases in moral decision-making
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract_snippet: Shows that LLMs exhibit amplified versions of known human cognitive biases in moral decision-making, establishing a new benchmark paradigm comparing AI to human cognitive baselines.

papers.title: A roadmap for evaluating moral competence in large language models
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes a comprehensive roadmap for evaluating moral competence in LLMs, defining key dimensions and metrics for next-generation moral evaluation benchmarks.

papers.title: ValuePrism: A Pluralistic Value Framework for AI
papers.abstract_snippet: Develops ValuePrism, a pluralistic value framework capturing 31,000+ values from diverse sources, enabling evaluation of AI systems against a broad spectrum of human values rather than single frameworks.

papers.title: One Model, Many Morals: Evaluating Moral Pluralism in LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Evaluates whether LLMs can represent and reason about multiple moral frameworks simultaneously, finding that models tend to collapse moral pluralism into dominant Western ethical perspectives.

papers.title: Structured Moral Reasoning in Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Evaluates structured moral reasoning capabilities in language models, analyzing how models decompose ethical problems and whether they follow principled reasoning chains.

papers.title: LLM Ethics Benchmark: Three-Dimensional Assessment of Moral Reasoning in Large Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes a three-dimensional framework for evaluating LLM ethical reasoning covering moral recognition, judgment, and action.

papers.title: MoralBench: Moral Evaluation of LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Proposes MoralBench for evaluating the moral reasoning capabilities of LLMs across diverse ethical scenarios.

papers.title: The Fragility of Moral Judgment in Large Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Demonstrates the fragility of moral judgments in LLMs under slight prompt variations, providing a new evaluation paradigm for testing robustness of moral reasoning.
